messages:
Anika: Quick follow-up on the SDK ergonomics RFC re: precision profiles — can we converge on a simpler surface for app devs? I'm worried the current API exposes too many low-level knobs.

Matt: +1. The current shape (PrecisionProfile { model, preferred_bits, fallback_chain }) is unintuitive for product teams.

Sam: Proposal: expose two layers in the SDK — a high-level `policy` (cost/quality tier) and an `advancedProfile` for power users. Default `policy = "balanced"`.

Jen: Policy names we can try: `low-latency`, `balanced`, `high-fidelity`. Each maps to a runtime mapping (e.g., balanced -> try fp8, then int8, fallback float).

Lee: We should define the telemetry contract now: `requested_policy`, `resolved_precision` (e.g., fp8/int8/float32), `fallback_chain`, `fallback_reason`, and a `quality_regression_score` slot if we compute quality deltas.

Anika: Agree. Also, keep backward compatibility — add `X-Precision-Policy` header and make the SDK set it. Existing `precision_profile` requests should still work and win over policy if provided.

Matt: SDK ergonomics example (short):

// high-level
client.generate({ prompt, precision: { policy: 'balanced' } })

// advanced
client.generate({ prompt, precision: { advancedProfile: { preferred_bits: 8, allow_fp8: true, fallbacks: ['int8','float32'] } } })

Sam: Runtime precedence: request-level advancedProfile > request-level policy > endpoint default profile > org default. Document this clearly.

Jen: For policy->profile mapping, we need a stable table in docs and a runtime implementation that can be updated without breaking SDKs (server-side mapping). We should version the mapping (mapping_v1, mapping_v2) and include the mapping id in responses.

Lee: Agree on versioning. Also: add a lightweight signal for quality-sensitive requests: `quality_target: 0.95` (0..1). Runtime can treat that as an intent, not a strict SLA. This helps routing and quant selection.

Anika: Good idea, but we should be careful to avoid per-request heavy evals. `quality_target` should influence routing and model selection only, not trigger synchronous quality checks.

Matt: Migration plan: SDK PR adds `precision.policy` field, sets header, and ships adapter that translates legacy `precision_profile` to the new shape. We'll add a deprecation warning in logs for 6 months.

Sam: Ops concerns: telemetry retention and debug surface — we need a sampling plan for detailed fallback traces (only on error or sampled 0.5% of requests) to avoid cost blowup.

ops-bot: CI note: added `precision.policy` to traces/otel, retention 30d for full traces, fallback traces sampled at 0.5%.

Jen: Tests: we need a small harness that runs a representative prompt suite across all policies and captures quality deltas and latency. Can be nightly and on PRs changing mapping.

Lee: Also add a guardrail in runtime: if a policy mapping would cause >X% quality regression on canary, block rollout and alert QA.

Anika: Action items: 1) Matt opens SDK PR with adapter + docs, 2) Matt/Lee create runtime mapping_v1 table and implement precedence, 3) Jen owns test harness and threshold checks, 4) Ops sets sampling/trace flags (thanks).

Matt: I'll open the PR this afternoon and ping reviewers in the RFC thread. Tagging @Jen @Lee for test/mapping sync.

Jen: Ack. I'll sketch the harness and share a short checklist for nightly runs.

Sam: LGTM. Keep the advancedProfile for power users, but document the policy-first flow in the Quickstart.

Anika: Thanks all. We'll iterate on policy names and mapping semantics in the PR comments. :thumbsup:
